question: deep-researcher ships a 4000-word visa-policy dossier straight to the client after a single Claude pass; it contains a hallucinated KBLI code and a miscalculated PPh21 figure that one adversarial reviewer would have caught. No second pair of eyes ran before publish.

A spec for the office-personal-channel-block was approved on the author's own read-through; the C4 tamper-detection design had a load-bearing flaw that a parallel Gemini+DeepSeek+Codex review would have flagged, but it shipped because the design 'seemed obvious'.

question: A wave session dispatched four peer agents with no orchestrator coordinating them; two independently edited the same deploy worktree and a third triggered a prod Fly deploy while a sibling was mid-migration, amplifying one small error across the whole batch.

question: WR2 hero-image step does cp ../test-1/placeholder-hero.jpg . to reuse an asset and writes image_source unset; twelve consecutive carousels ship the same 'paper on dark desk' hero. Filenames differed run-to-run so nobody noticed the bytes were identical.

Intel-lake reuses an embedding fragment from a prior run keyed only by document filename; the file was re-uploaded with edited content but the same name, so the pipeline serves stale vectors as if fresh. No content hash was compared before reuse.

CRM worker reports 'invoice email sent OK' and exits 0, but Brevo silently rejected the payload and zero emails left; the wrapper trusted the 200 from its own enqueue call and never queried Brevo's delivery status afterward to confirm the send actually happened.

wa-mirror cutover script logs 'migration applied: 5 tables' and exits 0; the migration transaction had actually rolled back, but the wrapper printed a hardcoded count instead of running SELECT against information_schema to confirm the tables exist on disk.

events_outbox consumer for CRM mutations does an HTTP POST to kita.balizero.com/inbox and moves on; during a rolling Fly deploy the endpoint 502s for 8s and those mutation events are dropped, because the producer fired directly instead of writing to a durable outbox drained by a separate retrying consumer.
ground_truth: Pattern 2: Durable queue / outbox / DLQ / replay contract

question: regulatory-watcher detects a new regulation delta and pg_notify's the briefing channel; the sole listener was restarting for a config reload at that instant, so the delta is lost forever and the morning briefing omits it. No replay log exists to recover the missed event.

question: post_publish_poller daemon's PID is alive and it logs a heartbeat every 30s, but it has been silently processing zero rows for 6 hours because its DB cursor wedged; monitoring only checks that the process exists and that a heartbeat line appears, never that the work-done metric is advancing.

evolver wrapper's psql probe returns empty stdout when flycast DNS fails to resolve; the wrapper interprets empty output as 'advisory lock held by another run' and exits 3, when in fact no run is holding the lock — it simply can't tell the DB is unreachable. There is no liveness check that the psql command itself succeeded.

memory-sync-bidirectional and nuz-sync both fire at the same minute and each opens a git push to the same feature branch; without an atomic claim on the sync slot they race and one push clobbers the other's ref. The fix is a single-flight lease on the sync key, not a bigger orchestration wave.
